author: kimi-code

scope.theme_definition_location: src/static/theme.css (CSS custom properties, one block per theme)
scope.theme_selection_location: src/app.py:82 THEMES tuple; persisted in localStorage 'dk-theme'; applied as html[data-theme] by src/templates/base.html:8-9 and src/static/theme.js
scope.centralization_verdict: Core palette IS centralized in theme.css variables and most UI consumes them. Gaps: per-template <style> blocks hard-code a few colors; share.py snapshot and monthly_print.html carry their own fixed palettes; no color-scheme declaration anywhere.

duplicate_check.conclusion: No previously reported issues exist, so no finding can be marked a potential duplicate. All findings below are NEW.

findings.title: Input placeholder text nearly unreadable in dark theme
findings.cause: No ::placeholder rule and no color-scheme declaration anywhere. Inputs get background var(--card) #161b22 in dark theme, while the UA default placeholder color stays light-scheme. Current Chromium UA stylesheet uses a fixed color: #757575 for placeholders (not rgba(0,0,0,0.6) as first assumed).
findings.fix_location: src/static/theme.css:324 (add ::placeholder rule using var(--muted); add color-scheme: light dark)

findings.title: Share page Generate button hover: white text on light blue
findings.cause: Hover sets background var(--blue) #4dabf7 with color var(--white) #ffffff in light theme.
findings.fix_note: Round 3 correction (R1): --on-accent alone does NOT fix light theme -- it is #ffffff there, still 2.48:1 on #4dabf7. Correct fix: background var(--accent) + color var(--on-accent) -> 5.17:1 light / 7.49:1 dark.

findings.title: Notification dropdown header text fails contrast in BOTH themes
findings.cause: .alert-dropdown-v3 .dd-head uses color var(--muted) on background var(--bar-muted).
findings.measured_contrast: light 3.28:1 (#6b7280 on #d1d5db), dark 3.97:1 (#8b949e on #30363d); both below 4.5:1 for 11px text

findings.title: Portfolio drawer facts table hard-codes a light border
findings.cause: border-bottom: 1px solid #dee2e6 is hard-coded; in dark theme it renders as a bright light-gray line on the dark drawer instead of var(--border) #30363d.

findings.title: Completed/Matured chip text marginally fails contrast in light theme
findings.cause: --matured-fg on --matured-bg for 12px semibold chip text.

findings.title: Danger chip text marginally fails contrast in light theme
findings.cause: --danger-fg on --danger-bg for 12px semibold chip text.
findings.measured_contrast: light 4.41:1 (#dc2626 on #fef2f2), dark 6.80:1 pass for .chip-danger; .chip-invalid drops to 4.42:1 dark due to opacity (see N4)

findings.title: Payment edit checkbox accent hard-coded blue
findings.cause: accent-color: #4dabf7 instead of var(--accent) (theme.css:344 already uses var(--accent) for other checkboxes).

findings.title: Share page checkboxes use the wrong blue token
findings.cause: accent-color: var(--blue) uses the cell-background token #4dabf7 instead of --accent, so light-theme checkboxes are a different blue from every button/toggle.

findings.title: Native form controls and scrollbars not themed in dark mode
findings.cause: No color-scheme declaration anywhere, so select dropdown popups, date-picker indicators (add_position.html uses input[type=date]) and scrollbars render in light-scheme colors while the page is dark.
findings.exact_colors: UA light-scheme defaults on dark surfaces

findings.title: Grid future-cell text color hard-coded
findings.cause: color: #adb5bd instead of var(--muted). Light theme contrast vs --card-bg is 1.87:1; currently the cell only renders a non-breaking space so no text is visible today, but any future content would be unreadable.

findings.title: Grid legend copy hard-codes light-theme hex values
findings.cause: Legend text says 'paid (green #d3f9d8)' and 'due (light red #ffc9c9)'; in dark theme the actual swatches are #10251a and #2b1519, so the labels are wrong.

findings.title: Links use browser default colors that fail the dark theme
findings.cause: No global anchor color rule, so links fall back to the UA default: unvisited -webkit-link #0000EE, visited #551A8B. These do not adapt to data-theme.
findings.measured_contrast: dark #0000EE on #161b22 = 1.84:1 unvisited, #551A8B on #161b22 = 1.57:1 visited (both FAIL); light theme passes
findings.fix_location: src/static/theme.css (add a { color: var(--accent) } rule); example src/templates/goals.html:37,42
findings.round3_correction: R1: original cause (inherits --text) and INFO severity were wrong; links use UA link colors and are near-invisible in dark theme.

findings.title: Card shadows hard-coded rgba(30,30,30,0.08)
findings.cause: Per-template shadows bypass theme variables; in dark theme the shadow is effectively invisible.

findings.title: Generated share snapshot carries its own fixed light palette
findings.cause: share.py embeds a standalone print-styled palette rather than reusing theme tokens. Acceptable for an offline print artifact, but it duplicates palette values with no single source.

findings.title: Monthly print view carries its own fixed light palette
findings.cause: Print output is intentionally fixed to paper-light colors; same duplication note as T14.

findings.title: Settings theme radio ignores stored theme on first paint
findings.cause: The 'system' radio is hard-coded checked regardless of localStorage; theme.js corrects it after load, so there is a brief wrong checked state.

findings.title: Central stylesheet hard-codes four black shadows
findings.cause: theme.css itself hard-codes box-shadow colors instead of theme tokens — same single-source-of-truth gap as T13, including invisible-in-dark-theme behavior. Found in review.

findings.title: Shipped v1.0 build has the pre-fix dark --white token
findings.cause: product/dk_bond_tracker_v1.0/src/static/theme.css still carries dark --white: #ffffff (the #161b22 surface fix from commit cd22dff never made it into the shipped copy). In the shipped dark theme every var(--white) surface (share panel, payout meta, payment-edit card, add-position card, position drawer, payout-cell hover, payment inputs) renders true white under #e6edf3 text.

findings.title: Watchlist fact labels fail contrast in light theme
findings.cause: .fact-label uses var(--muted) inside .details-row td whose background is var(--header-row).

findings.title: Invalid chip fails contrast in BOTH themes due to opacity
findings.cause: .chip-invalid applies opacity: 0.75 on top of the danger token pair, dragging effective contrast below threshold.
findings.measured_contrast: light 3.27:1 (#dc2626@0.75 over #fef2f2), dark 4.42:1 (#ff7b72@0.75 over #2b1519); both FAIL
findings.exact_colors: light #dc2626 on #fef2f2 at opacity 0.75; dark #ff7b72 on #2b1519 at opacity 0.75

findings.title: On-going token pair fails contrast in light theme
findings.cause: --ongoing-fg #16a34a on --ongoing-bg #f0fdf4, used by .chip-ongoing (theme.css:306, 12px semibold) and .banner-success (theme.css:509-512, 13px, live via app.js:93 + settings.html:82). Dark passes at 8.37:1.
findings.measured_contrast: light 3.15:1 (FAIL, worse than T5 4.39 and T6 4.41); dark 8.37:1 pass

findings.title: color-scheme: light dark at :root follows the OS, not the selected theme
findings.cause: The T1/T9 recommended fix (color-scheme: light dark on :root) makes UA controls follow OS preference; a light-OS user who manually picks Dark still gets light select popups, date indicators and scrollbars.
findings.fix_location: src/static/theme.css — scope it: html[data-theme="dark"] { color-scheme: dark } html[data-theme="light"] { color-scheme: light } html[data-theme="system"] { color-scheme: light dark }
